system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Status:** Internal and privileged. Not for circulation to Harbourglass Ventures or its counsel.

## Overview

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every point. Several departures matter more than they first appear:

- **Hidden overrides.** Clause 12.3/13 says any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise." Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature." Together these would quietly pull fraud, title, tax, IP and specific indemnities into the general regime.
- **The covering letter contradicts the Disclosure Letter.** The Update says Bluefen is "addressed." The Disclosure Letter says no final Bluefen consent and no evidence of its conditions has been supplied.
- **The disclosure base is stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. All factual positions (Riverlark payout, Bluefen, Ironquay, DD-006) need a refresh before we rely on them.
- **Labels are not substance.** We should not accept descriptions such as "fair and balanced," "settled," "adequate," "addressed" or "not expected to be material" on the Seller's say-so (playbook s0.4/6.3).

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4,800,000. **Reject; revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- AUD 4.8m is exactly our conditional fallback. That match does not make it acceptable. The fallback can be used only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given.
- Do not signal that the fallback exists. If the team wants to move, seek Amelia's written authority first, tied specifically to this draft. Even then, assess the cap together with the thresholds, time limits and carve-outs below, because the package as a whole is far worse than a 20% cap alone.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2). **Reject.**

| | Playbook | Seller |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 5,000 | AUD 25,000 (5x) |
| Basket | AUD 50,000 | AUD 250,000 (5x) |
| Mechanism | Tipping: first dollar recoverable once exceeded | Deductible: excess only |

The deductible structure alone permanently removes AUD 250,000 of recoverable loss. Combined with the higher de minimis, which screens out each claim before it can count toward the basket, many genuine claims would never be recoverable. Revert to 5k / 50k with first-dollar recovery.

### 1.3 Time limits (cl 12.3/13). **Reject.**
- 18 months is our fallback and also needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which we do not have. Revert to **24 months**.
- The words "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" are a hidden general-regime override. Delete them. Each category (Title/Capacity, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenants, fraud) should carry its own express regime and should not depend on our remembering to carve it out each time.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties. **Reject outright.**
"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title at 20% of price for 18 months. Our position is a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar. If title fails we have not bought the company, so a 20% cap is commercially indefensible.

### 1.5 Fraud and limitations/reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). **Reject; non-negotiable.**
- Applying caps, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" would, on its face, cover fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- Insert an express carve-out: none of the limitations, caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provisions applies to fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller, the Company or their officers, employees or advisers, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **No one on our team may waive this.** Also exclude specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants from the general limitations.

### 1.6 Tax and IP ("settled under the general regime"). **Reject.**
These terms are **open**, not settled. Do not concede that Tax or IP warranties fall within the 20% cap or the 18-month period. We are also not asserting unlimited liability. We should simply record that they remain under negotiation as separate categories.

---

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2). **Reject.**
- Clause 1.1 deems the whole data room disclosed. Clause 1.2 deems the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" disclosed. Both contradict our requirement for specific, fair disclosure.
- Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Only matters disclosed fairly, specifically and with enough detail for the Buyer to identify their nature and scope, against the specific warranty, should qualify the warranties.
- Clause 1.4 (no admission) is acceptable in principle. However, it must not be read to undercut specific indemnities or the Completion conditions. For example, it must not support an argument that no consent was "legally required."

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3). **Reject; delete.**
- This is a blanket exclusion: knowledge of "the Buyer or its advisers," including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. It would turn our due diligence against us and gut the specific indemnities. We already know about Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses and DD-006, so this clause could defeat claims on exactly the issues we are protecting against.
- If any qualifier survives, it should apply only to **Seller** awareness, limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Specific transaction issues

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3). **Reject the drafting.**
- Bluefen is roughly AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). This is a material customer.
- The Update's claim that consent is "addressed" is contradicted by Disclosure Letter item 2. There is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied.
- "Reasonable endeavours" is insufficient under our playbook. "Satisfied on delivery of written consent" would let Completion proceed even if the consent is conditional or its conditions remain unmet.
- **Required:** a Condition Precedent requiring an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, plus evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that the cl 11.3 conditions are met before Completion. The Buyer alone should be able to waive the condition.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7). **Reject.**
- "Approximately AUD 3.2m" is not a payout figure. A "release to be provided following Completion" leaves us owning a company whose assets remain encumbered.
- **Required:**
  - a current payout letter (dated close to Completion, with per diem);
  - direct repayment from Completion funds to Riverlark, recorded in the funds flow;
  - executed releases and discharges of security, and PPSR releases, delivered at Completion;
  - treatment of the facility as Debt in the price mechanics.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, so do not offer this route.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses: DD-005, AUD 420,000. **Reject the silent exclusion.**
- The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller," but they are not in the funds flow. If the Company pays them, the economic cost falls on us after Completion.
- The Disclosure Letter is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Required:** a specific funds-flow line item or Debt-like deduction for AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs** (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG handling), or an express Seller funding obligation backed by a specific indemnity. We also need confirmation of how the continued-employment conditions are tested.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1). **Reject "adequate."**
- An indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment covers only one route to loss. It does not cover failure of the assignment, third-party IP claims, delay or re-development cost, or loss of use of the Project Materials.
- **Required:** a broader IP indemnity covering any loss from Company ownership of, or right to use, the Ironquay deliverables. The SOW3 cure should be preserved: the Seller procures cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and delivers a confirmatory assignment before Completion, or the matter becomes a funds-flow item.
- The AUD 180,000 open amount comes from DD-010 and is **not** independently bank-verified in either direction. Request Ironquay's own statement or a bank-verified position. Do not treat 180k as a confirmed debt or as a cap.

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006). **Do not accept "not expected to be material"; do not overstate it either.**
- On the record we have: about 1,240 records may be involved, and a link was sent to an unintended external address. It is **not established** whether anyone accessed the file, what the exact scope is, or whether notification is required.
- We should **not** assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss. The Seller's materiality conclusion is equally unsupported.
- **Required:**
  - a covenant to preserve all logs and evidence;
  - completion of an appropriate investigation, potentially by an independent forensic provider;
  - regular updates to the Buyer and Buyer consultation on any notification decision;
  - a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident (including regulatory, notification and remediation costs), outside the general cap and basket;
  - a refresh of facts since 22 September.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000). **Assess; do not concede either way.**
- The Seller calls them "ordinary course." The Disclosure Letter itself says it does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course, and that the three should be read together.
- Our playbook does **not** treat them as automatic Debt or a price deduction.
- **Action:** request the contracts and the timing, terminability and accrual position for each. Decide on treatment (working capital, Debt, specific indemnity, or no adjustment) on the evidence.

### 3.7 Title (DD-012). **Reject as sole evidence.**
- DD-012 is the Company's own internal register, supplied by the Seller. The Disclosure Letter itself says the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Required:** independent evidence. This includes:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share issue and transfer history, with board minutes;
  - share certificates (or confirmation that the shares are uncertificated);
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the shares;
  - releases of any encumbrances;
  - evidence of the Seller's corporate authority and capacity to sell (board resolution, constitution check, no pre-emption or third-party rights).

### 3.8 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Disclosure Letter characterises these as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not change-of-control consents. That is plausible but is the Seller's reading. Our team should confirm it against the actual clauses, add the lease notification to Completion deliverables, and add a warranty that no change-of-control consent is required under either contract.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / 6.0m.** Fallback not authorised; do not reveal it. |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k, excess only | **5k / 50k, first dollar** |
| 3 | General claims period | 18 months | **24 months.** 18 months not authorised. |
| 4 | "Applies to all Claims" override | Included | **Delete.** Separate express regimes per category. |
| 5 | Title/Capacity | Same as general | **100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge** |
| 6 | Fraud | Swept into all limitations | **Full carve-out. Non-negotiable.** |
| 7 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Open.** Separate categories; no concession. |
| 8 | Disclosure | Whole data room plus public records | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket bar incl. advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete.** Any fallback limited to named Seller persons plus reasonable enquiry; never title, capacity, fraud or indemnities. |
| 10 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | **CP:** effective consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met; Buyer-only waiver |
| 11 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | **Current payout, direct repayment at Completion, releases delivered at Completion** |
| 12 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item or Seller-funded,** including all on-costs |
| 13 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity "adequate" | **Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure;** verify 180k independently |
| 14 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preserve, investigate, update, specific indemnity.** No assumed breach or quantum. |
| 15 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Assess on evidence;** no automatic Debt treatment |
| 16 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | **Independent verification required** |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | **Verify against source clauses;** add warranty |

## 5. Process points

1. **Authority.** Nothing in this package triggers our fallbacks. If the team wants to use the 20% cap or the 18-month period, obtain Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this specific draft. Until then, our mark-up should state our starting positions.
2. **Information requests to the Seller now:**
   - Riverlark payout letter;
   - Bluefen consent status and cl 11.3 conditions evidence;
   - Ironquay statement or payment evidence and the assignment;
   - DD-006 investigation update since 22 September;
   - Sandbar contracts;
   - bonus on-cost calculation;
   - independent title evidence;
   - DD-007 and DD-009 clause text.
3. **Do not rely on stale facts.** Ask for a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter to a current date, and distinguish verified updates from Seller assertions as they come in.
4. **Mark-up approach.** Respond with a full mark-up restoring our positions. Do not trade individual points in correspondence: the Seller's package interlocks, and conceding one item (for example, the override wording) undermines several others.
=== END ADVICE ===
